title: ICSE CLASS 6 — English | Verbs Tenses
description: Subject-wise test on Verbs Tenses (English) for ICSE CLASS 6. 25Q.
subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Identify the tense of the sentence: "The sun rises in the east every morning."

options.explanation: This tense is used for actions happening now, not universal truths.
This tense is used for completed actions in the past, not universal truths.
This tense is used for universal truths, habitual actions, and facts.
This tense is used for future actions, not universal truths.

questions.explanation: The sentence describes a universal truth and habitual action, which is typically expressed in the Present Simple Tense.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb: "Yesterday, my brother ______ a new storybook." (buy)

options.explanation: This is the present simple form of the verb, not the past form.
This is the simple past form of the verb "buy".
This is the present participle form of the verb, not the simple past form.
This is the future simple form of the verb, not the past form.

questions.explanation: The word "Yesterday" indicates the action happened in the past, so the simple past form of "buy" is used.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: "Tomorrow, we ______ to the zoo with our family."

options.explanation: This is the past simple form of the verb, not the future form.
This is the present simple form of the verb, not the future form.
While this could be used for future plans, the simple future tense is more direct and commonly used at the Class 6 level.
This is the simple future tense, correctly indicating an action that will happen in the future.

questions.explanation: The word "Tomorrow" indicates a future action, so the simple future tense is used.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is in the Present Continuous Tense?

options.text: She reads a book every night.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Simple Tense, describing a habitual action.
This sentence is in the Past Simple Tense, describing a completed action in the past.

options.text: He is watching television right now.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Continuous Tense, describing an action happening at the moment of speaking.

options.text: We will visit our grandparents next week.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the Future Simple Tense, describing an action that will happen in the future.

questions.explanation: The Present Continuous Tense describes an action happening at the moment of speaking, using "is/am/are" + verb-ing.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the appropriate tense: "While I ______ my homework, my phone suddenly ______." (do, ring)

options.explanation: The first verb should be in the past continuous tense to describe the ongoing action.
The second verb should be in the simple past tense to describe the sudden completed action.
This combination correctly uses the past continuous tense for the ongoing action and the simple past tense for the completed action.
This combination incorrectly uses the present participle and the present simple tense.

questions.explanation: The sentence describes an ongoing action in the past (doing homework) interrupted by a sudden completed action (phone rang).
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the Present Perfect Tense:

options.explanation: The use of "yesterday" requires the simple past tense, not the present perfect tense.
This sentence correctly uses the present perfect tense to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past and has a present result.

options.text: We have been going to the market now.
options.explanation: The present perfect continuous tense is incorrectly used with the time marker "now"; it should describe an action starting in the past and continuing up to the present.

options.text: They have played cricket next Sunday.
options.explanation: The present perfect tense cannot be used with a future time marker like "next Sunday".

questions.explanation: The Present Perfect Tense describes an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past or started in the past and continues to the present.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Transform the sentence from Simple Present to Simple Past Tense: "My brother writes beautiful poems."

options.text: My brother is writing beautiful poems.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.
This sentence is in the Simple Past Tense, with the main verb changed to its past simple form.

options.text: My brother will write beautiful poems.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the Future Simple Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

options.text: My brother has written beautiful poems.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Perfect Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

questions.explanation: To change a sentence from Simple Present to Simple Past, the main verb needs to be changed to its past simple form.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Select the best option to complete the sentence, describing an action that will be ongoing in the future: "This time tomorrow, I ______ on a beach in Goa."

options.explanation: This is the present simple form of the verb, not the future continuous form.
This is the past simple form of the verb, not the future continuous form.
This is the future simple form of the verb, not the future continuous form.
This is the future continuous form of the verb, correctly describing an action that will be ongoing at a specific point in the future.

questions.explanation: The phrase "This time tomorrow" indicates a specific point in the future when an action will be in progress, requiring the Future Continuous Tense.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Assertion: The sentence "They were playing football yesterday afternoon" is in the Past Continuous Tense. Reason: This tense is used to describe an action that was ongoing at a specific time in the past.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
options.explanation: The assertion is true because the sentence is indeed in the Past Continuous Tense, and the reason is true because it correctly explains the use of the Past Continuous Tense.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is NOT the correct explanation for Assertion.
options.explanation: The reason provided does correctly explain why the sentence is in the Past Continuous Tense.

options.text: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
options.explanation: The reason provided is true and explains the use of the Past Continuous Tense.

options.text: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true because the sentence is indeed in the Past Continuous Tense.

questions.explanation: The assertion correctly identifies the tense as Past Continuous, and the reason correctly explains the usage of the Past Continuous tense.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Read the paragraph and choose the option that best completes the blanks to maintain the correct tense for the narrative flow: "Last Sunday, my family and I ______ (1) to the park. The sun ______ (2) brightly, and many children ______ (3) kites."

options.explanation: These options are in the present tense, not the past tense required for the narrative.
While "was shining" and "were flying" are correct, "gone" is not the correct form of the verb to use here; it should be the simple past "went".
This option correctly uses the simple past "went" for the main action, and the past continuous "was shining" and "were flying" for the ongoing actions at that time.
While "shone" and "flew" could be used in some contexts, they do not provide as clear a picture of ongoing actions as the past continuous tense does.

questions.explanation: The narrative is set in the past, indicated by "Last Sunday", so all verbs should be in the past tense.

questions.question: Which word correctly completes the sentence: 'The Earth _____ around the Sun.'?

options.explanation: This is the Simple Past tense, which is incorrect for a general truth.
This is the Present Continuous tense, which is incorrect for a general truth.
This is the Simple Present tense, correct for a general truth.
This is the Simple Future tense, which is incorrect for a general truth.

questions.explanation: This sentence describes a universal truth or habitual action, which requires the Simple Present tense. 'Moves' is the correct form for the third person singular subject 'The Earth'.

questions.question: Which word correctly completes the sentence: 'Look! The children _____ in the park right now.'?

options.explanation: This is the Simple Present tense, which does not indicate an action happening now.
This is the Simple Past tense, which does not indicate an action happening now.
This is the Present Continuous tense, correct for an action happening now.
This is the Simple Future tense, which does not indicate an action happening now.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'right now' indicates an action happening at the moment of speaking. This requires the Present Continuous tense, which is formed with 'is/am/are' + verb-ing.
questions.hint: Look for time expressions that indicate the action is happening now.

questions.question: Which word correctly completes the sentence: 'I _____ my lunch before my friend arrived.'?

options.explanation: This is the Simple Present tense, which is incorrect for past actions.
This is the Present Perfect tense, which is incorrect for past actions with a specific time marker.
This is the Past Perfect tense, correct for an action completed before another past action.
This is the Present Continuous tense, which is incorrect for past actions.

questions.explanation: This sentence describes two past actions. The action that happened earlier ('eating lunch') should be in the Past Perfect tense, while the later action ('friend arrived') is in the Simple Past tense.
questions.hint: Identify the sequence of past actions and use the correct tense for the earlier action.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Which word correctly completes the sentence: 'She _____ her grandmother next weekend.'?

options.explanation: This is the base form of the verb, which is incorrect without an auxiliary verb.
This is the Simple Past tense, which is incorrect for a future event.
This is the Present Continuous tense for future, which is less direct than 'will visit'.
This is the Simple Future tense, correct for a planned future event.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'next weekend' indicates a future action. The Simple Future tense, formed with 'will' + base verb, is appropriate for planned future events.
questions.hint: Look for time expressions that indicate a future event.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the verb tense?

options.text: I have finished my homework yesterday.
options.explanation: This sentence incorrectly uses the Present Perfect tense with a definite past time marker.
This sentence correctly uses the Simple Past tense with a definite past time marker.

options.text: I am finishing my homework yesterday.
options.explanation: This sentence incorrectly uses the Present Continuous tense with a definite past time marker.

options.text: I had finished my homework yesterday.
options.explanation: This sentence incorrectly uses the Past Perfect tense with a definite past time marker.

questions.explanation: The specific past time marker 'yesterday' requires the use of the Simple Past tense. The Present Perfect tense (A) and Past Perfect tense (D) are incorrect when a definite past time is mentioned. The Present Continuous (C) is also incorrect as the action is completed in the past.
questions.hint: Look for time expressions that specify a definite past time.
